newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 22.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
NEW PRIME MINISTER KEEPS OLD CABINET

A 35-member United Front ministry headed by Inder Kumar Gujral assumed office. Barring the food minister and four ministers of the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC), all members of the old government were retained. The TMC has decided not to participate in the government but extend support from the outside. The TMC ministers who do not figure in the Gujral ministry include P. Chidambaram and M. Arunachalam who held the finance and labour portfolios, respectively.
The Economic Times
RBI ASKS FOR TRANSPARENT POLICY ON CREDIT DISBURSAL

The Reserve Bank of India has asked commercial banks to lay down transparent policy guidelines for dispensing credit to the commercial sector. The banks have also been asked to include details about each broad category of economic activity and the policy they would follow for each of them.
BANKS FREE TO ADOPT SYNDICATE ROUTE FOR CREDIT

The Reserve Bank of India, while observing that syndication was an internationally practised model for financing credit requirements, has allowed banks the freedom to adopt the syndication route, irrespective of the quantum of credit involved if the arrangement suited the borrower and the financing banks. The international experience has been the driving force behind the RBI's decision to withdraw all mandatory stipulations on formation of consortia for working capital finance under the multiple banking arrangement.
PRIME MINISTER, CONGRESS TO DISCUSS CHANGES IN FINANCE BILL

Although there are no doubts over the passage of the budget, speculation is rife over changes that might be effected in the finance and appropriation bills. In the new situation, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, who also holds the finance portfolio, was expected to hold discussions with the Congress party on the changes to be introduced in the Finance Bill. Gujral has informed the joint business advisory committee of parliament that he was in favour of having the same finance bill reintroduced.
HINDALCO TO FLOAT $48 MLN FOREIGN BORROWING TRANCHE

Hindalco Industries, an Aditya Birla group company, will launch a $48 million external commercial borrowing (ECB) transaction. The issue was being arranged by ANZ Grindlays Bank and Citibank. Sources said the ECB tranche comprised an infrastructure component along with corporate expansion. The issue was being made for part financing the company's $500 million aluminium capacity expansion along with its $60 million captive power plant project.
Financial Express
BOURSE GREETS NEW PRIME MINISTER WITH 103 POINT JUMP

Stock markets greeted the new prime minister with a strong rally which brought share prices and indices above the pre-March 30 levels. The rally was spearheaded by foreign institutional investors who were waiting for the dust to settle on the political front. The Bombay bourse index closed at 3,799.79, up 103.27 points from the previous close and 133.45 points above the closing on March 28, the last trading day before the Congress withdrew support.
ONGC WILLING TO BUYOUT 60 PCT GOVERNMENT STAKE IN LUBRIZOL

The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) is keen on buying out the government's 60 percent stake in Lubrlzol India. The decision followed the government's intention to offload its entire holding in the company. The balance is held by Lubrizol Corporation of the United States, which eventually would like to hold a 50 percent stake with the new partner. Sources said ONGC would have to fork out one billion rupees to procure the holding at book value.
